method.m1: The main text was taken from the PDF (pp. {from}–{to}), without the table of contents, headings, tables, figure captions and the reference list, and split into {sentences} sentences. The reference list was analysed separately – it was used to check whether a source and its authors are cited in the document.
method.m2: Each sentence (longer ones in overlapping parts of up to 30 words) was searched in a web search engine. The result fragments were compared with the sentence; sources with a long shared word sequence or several matches were downloaded. If a website blocked access, the text was looked for in open scholarly databases (Europe PMC, Crossref, Unpaywall) and in the web archive (Wayback Machine).
method.m3: When enabled, every entry of the reference list was additionally looked up in scholarly databases; the texts or abstracts found were compared with the entire document.
method.m4: Each downloaded source was compared with all sentences of the document, not only those found by the search. Matches are classified as: verbatim (≥90 % of the sentence's words match in continuous sequences), minor edits (60–90 %), partial (35–60 % with a shared sequence of at least 6 words), possible paraphrase (≥60 % shared content words).
method.m5: The publication date of each source was determined from Crossref data, page metadata, the address, search engine data and the web archive. Sources later than the document cannot be plagiarism sources – usually they took the text from the document themselves.
method.m6: Each pair of matches was assessed in context: whether the text was taken verbatim without a reference, whether the author is cited but quotation marks are missing, or whether it is a paraphrase, a proper quotation, a common phrase or a coincidental match. Conclusions were drawn for each source and overall.
method.l1: Only sources available online were checked: paywalled articles, books and non-digitised publications may have remained unchecked.
method.l2: Free paraphrasing and translation from another language are detected only partly.
method.l3: The final decision on plagiarism must be made by a person who has reviewed the match pairs presented.

recommend.title: Strongly recommended: Serper search and an AI model
recommend.lead: Plagiarism works without them, but the results are much weaker. With a Serper key and an Anthropic or OpenAI key the check runs faster, finds more sources and labels matches far more accurately.
recommend.serper_text: Serper searches Google, so it finds more sources and works faster than the free DuckDuckGo search, which is slower, returns fewer results and may be rate-limited. New accounts get 2,500 free queries, then about $1 per 1,000.
recommend.llm_title: AI model – Anthropic or OpenAI (not set up)
recommend.llm_text: The AI model reads every match in context and decides whether it is a proper quotation, a paraphrase with a reference or text taken without a reference, and writes the conclusions. Without it matches are labelled automatically by similarity only, which is less accurate. A 200-page thesis costs about $0.50–1.50 with Claude Sonnet.
recommend.footer: Keys are kept in your computer's credential store. You can add them in Settings at any time.

wizard.welcome_text: Plagiarism checks a thesis or another long document for text taken from online sources without proper references, and builds a clear report you can share.
wizard.how1: Add a PDF. The text is read on your computer.
wizard.how2: Every sentence is searched on the web; the sources found are downloaded and compared with the whole document.
wizard.how3: An AI model (optional) assesses each match in context: quotation, paraphrase, copied without a reference…
wizard.how4: You get an interactive report and can export it as PDF, CSV, JSON or HTML.
wizard.search_text: The search engine finds the web pages that may contain the document's sentences. A Serper key is recommended: it is the most thorough. Without a key the free DuckDuckGo search is used – it works, but it is slower and finds less.
wizard.llm_text: An AI model reads every match pair and decides whether it is a proper quotation, a paraphrase with a reference or text taken without a reference, and writes the conclusions. Without it the matches are labelled automatically from their similarity only.
wizard.llm_none: You can skip this step: the check still works, the labels are just less precise.
wizard.done_text: Optionally add your e-mail for Unpaywall – it helps to find open-access versions of scholarly articles. Everything can be changed later in Settings.

about.lead: A free tool for checking theses and other long documents for plagiarism from online sources.
about.author: Author
about.privacy1: The PDF and the report stay on your computer.
about.privacy2: Sentences of the document are sent to the search engine you choose (Serper, Tavily or DuckDuckGo).
about.privacy3: If AI assessment is on, the matching passages and the source excerpts are sent to the AI provider (Anthropic or OpenAI).
about.privacy4: Nothing is sent to the authors of Plagiarism; there is no telemetry.
about.limits: Only sources available online are checked: paywalled articles, books and non-digitised publications may be missed. Translation from another language and free paraphrasing are detected only partly. The report is an aid – the final decision must be made by a person who has reviewed the matches.
